communityVoices.quote: starting with Estimated Prophet, the 2nd set of this show basically takes on a life of it's own. A high energy, rock & roll romp that really defies the senses.
Donna Jean some pretty augghs during Estimated.
jerry is just redonkuluous this evening. His guitar just sings all night and even though his voice has sounded better on many a night, damn if he doesn't give it 110% on the vocals this night.

This show ranks #12 in Deadbase's tape ranking, and with very good reason (I'd give it extra stars for this review if I could). Recording quality is terrific, the set list is phenomenal, and Jerry is ON in a big way for both vocals and lead.
Though I can't say this show is my favorite of '78, that may be either be 4/12 or 1/22 and the Dick's Picks Vol. 18 pastiche of 2/03 and 2/05.

whyThisShow: This show is officially released as 'Red Rocks: 7/8/78' and sits at number 12 in Deadbase's tape rankings [source: 'This show ranks #12 in Deadbase’s tape ranking, and with very good reason']. The second set is the engine — one reviewer described the stretch from Estimated Prophet through Sugar Magnolia as "too good for words, honestly I can't even describe it" [source: 'The jamming from Estimated all the way through Sugar Magnolia is too good for words, honestly I can’t even describe it']. Jerry's guitar gets specific praise across multiple reviews: one listener noted that "Jerry's guitar lines dance in the Estimated> Other One> Eyes and soar during Wharf Rat" [source: 'Jerry’s guitar lines dance in the Estimated> Other One> Eyes and soar during Wharf Rat']. Keith Godchaux also draws notice — one reviewer who was still getting into the '78 period found him "sick on this show, really on fire" [source: 'Keith & Jerry still sound good together here']. One dissenting voice points out that other '78 dates — 4/12 and 1/22 — may edge this one out [source: 'that may be either be 4/12 or 1/22 and the Dick’s Picks Vol. 18 pastiche of 2/03 and 2/05'], but the weight of community opinion puts this night firmly in the year's top tier.
listenFor: The Estimated Prophet into Other One into Eyes of the World sequence is the heart of the show — one reviewer described how Jerry "alternately transitions from chopping to floating in butterfly-like fashion during the lead jams" in the Eyes [source: 'Jerry alternately transitions from chopping to floating in butterfly-like fashion during the lead jams']. The Wharf Rat is singled out repeatedly: one reviewer called it "unlike any other version of Wharf Rat that exists" and specifically flagged Jerry's quiet "Ssshhh" mid-song as "priceless" [source: 'Jerry’s “Ssshhh” in the middle of the “back on my feet someday” refrain is priceless']. The Franklin's Tower that follows is rare post-drums placement, and one listener called it "a raging jam throughout" [source: 'the Franklin’s Tower is a raging jam throughout']. The encores go three deep — Terrapin into One More Saturday Night into Werewolves of London — and one reviewer noted "you can tell they are having a good time doing this tune" on the Zevon cover [source: 'You can tell they are having a good time doing this tune']. The soundboard recording rewards the volume advice one reviewer repeated twice: "it demands to be played loud" [source: 'It demands to be played loud'].
context: This is a soundboard recording (identifier: gd78-07-08.sbd.unknown.294.sbeok.shnf) from the era-77-peak classification, one of two consecutive Red Rocks nights that the community treats as a single run. The show was officially released by the band's organization as 'Red Rocks: 7/8/78,' confirming its canonical standing. Keith and Donna Godchaux were still in the lineup; the Godchaux era would end the following year. One reviewer noted that "the guys I hung around seemed to consist of quite a number of Dead Heads" who were circulating this tape as early as 1979, suggesting it traveled the lot quickly [source: 'I first listened to this tape in the Fall of 1979'].
funFact: One listener reported that after three days at Red Rocks in 1985, he "started going to a lot of Rainbow Gatherings" because the venue itself had that kind of effect on him [source: 'After the 3rd day at Red Rocks in 85. I started going to a lot of Rainbow Gatherings because I realized I was connecting not only to GD but I was also influenced by the hand of GOD on nature'].
headline: Red Rocks, July '78, second set wide open.
